Growth as the job is to connect users to the value of your product. Growth sometimes gets this reputation that it's just pure metrics hacking.

Lenny Rachitsky (00:00:08):
You've worked at three of the most successful consumer subscription products in the world. What do you think is the biggest missing piece that people don't get about building a successful consumer subscription product?

Albert Cheng (00:00:18):
User retention is gold for consumer subscription companies. If you don't retain your users, then a lot of the onus is on getting them to pay on day one.

Lenny Rachitsky (00:00:26):
Noam Levinsky, he said that I need to ask you about the biggest monetization win that you found at Grammarly.

Albert Cheng (00:00:31):

Lenny Rachitsky (00:00:50):
What's the most counterintuitive lesson you've learned about building teams?

Albert Cheng (00:00:54):
I saw some of the highest performers just being people that had very high agency, had that clock speed, had that energy, but they didn't necessarily need to have deep experience on that matter. # Unlocking Product Growth: A Guide to Connecting Users to Value

## Understanding Product Growth

Product growth is not just about metrics hacking; it's about connecting users to the value of your product. This means getting the right people to experience the product in a way that makes them dependent on it.   

## Definition of Product Growth and Its Core Objective

Product growth is defined as connecting users to the value of your product. It's not just about pure metrics hacking. It's about getting as many of the right people to experience the product in a way where they'd be very disappointed if they could no longer use it. This is not just acquisition, but also about trying to get people to experience the product in a way that makes them dependent on it.   

## Prerequisite of Product-Market Fit Before Initiating Growth Efforts

Before initiating growth efforts, it's essential to have product-market fit. This means having a product that users love, showing strong signs of retention, or having a good loop that you can start thinking about growth. If you start growing a product without product-market fit, you're actually doing more damage than good. You want a product that's tight and has product-market fit to start building the flywheel and start growing.  

## Strategy of Incremental Improvements and High-Volume Experimentation

A strategy of incremental improvements and high-volume experimentation involves focusing on the small things that add up to big things. It's not about having a perfect plan, but about shipping multiple things and seeing what works. Growth is a game of inches, and it's about moving things 1% faster every single week. Sometimes, it's the small things that matter the most.   

## Building a Value Delivery Engine and Flywheel Around Must-Have Value

To build a value delivery engine and flywheel around must-have value, you need to understand the problem, figure out a metric that captures units of that value being delivered, and then diagram all the different ways to grow that metric. This involves looking at onboarding, engagement loops, and other aspects of the product.   

## Distinction Between Organic Virality from Product Value and Synthetic Virality

Organic virality comes from the product value, while synthetic virality is often superficial and fails. Products that try to be viral just for the sake of it tend to fail. Instead, focus on building a great product that solves a sharp problem.  

## Warning Against Relying on Out-of-Context Growth Hacks and Shortcuts

Relying on out-of-context growth hacks and shortcuts is often a recipe for disaster. People are grasping for shortcuts that are completely out of context or specific to one example and don't apply as a pattern or to their type of business.  

## Key Components Required to Implement a Product-Led Growth (PLG) Motion

To implement a product-led growth (PLG) motion, you need to provide something free and self-serve, have a quick time to value, a self-serve checkout experience, a data foundation, and simple pricing that people understand. This allows the B2B buyer to buy your software in a PLG motion.  

## Approach to Finding Growth Opportunities in Existing Mature Products

When finding growth opportunities in existing mature products, consider why people are using the product and where the areas of growth are. Even in complex systems, there's usually a part that's growing, a part that's mature, and a part that's declining. Look for these areas and explore how to grow them.

To achieve product growth, focus on connecting users to the value of your product. Finally, consider why people are using the product and where the areas of growth are, and explore how to grow them.

To build a value delivery engine and flywheel around must-have value, you need to understand the problem, figure out a metric that captures units of that value being delivered, and then diagram all the different ways to grow that metric. This involves looking at onboarding, engagement loops, and other aspects of the product.   

## Distinction Between Organic Virality from Product Value and Synthetic Virality

Organic virality comes from the product value, while synthetic virality is often superficial and fails. Products that try to be viral just for the sake of it tend to fail. Instead, focus on building a great product that solves a sharp problem.  

## Warning Against Relying on Out-of-Context Growth Hacks and Shortcuts

Relying on out-of-context growth hacks and shortcuts is often a recipe for disaster. People are grasping for shortcuts that are completely out of context or specific to one example and don't apply as a pattern or to their type of business.  

## Key Components Required to Implement a Product-Led Growth (PLG) Motion

To implement a product-led growth (PLG) motion, you need to provide something free and self-serve, have a quick time to value, a self-serve checkout experience, a data foundation, and simple pricing that people understand. This allows the B2B buyer to buy your software in a PLG motion.  

## Approach to Finding Growth Opportunities in Existing Mature Products

When finding growth opportunities in existing mature products, consider why people are using the product and where the areas of growth are. Even in complex systems, there's usually a part that's growing, a part that's mature, and a part that's declining. Look for these areas and explore how to grow them.
